plain_english: Now the eighth chapter. Arjuna said: What is that Brahman? What is the self? What is action, O supreme person? What is said to be concerning beings? And what is called the divine?
sanskrit_cite: atha aṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   kiṃ tad brahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama | adhibhūtaṃ ca  kiṃ proktamadhidaivaṃ kimucyate

plain_english: How is the supreme sacrifice, and who is here in this body, O Madhusūdana? At the time of departure, how are you knowable by those of controlled selves? They know Brahman and so forth. By such questions raised by the Lord, preceded by nine questions, the matter is determined. The remainder is: how does the supreme sacrifice stand in the body?
sanskrit_cite: adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra dehe'smin madhusūdana | prayāṇakāle ca  kathaṃ jñeyo'si niyatātmabhiḥ | te brahma tadviduḥ ityādinā yadbhagavatopakṣiptaṃ  tatpraśnanavakapūrvakaṃ nirṇayati | adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko'tra  dehe tiṣṭhatīti śeṣaḥ

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: the supreme imperishable Brahman, whose own nature is called the inner self, is emission named action, causing the birth of beings' states; because of its greatness and expansion it is denoted by the word inner self; consciousness-being, whose nature is unceasing dharma, is Brahman unlimited externally, and through sovereign freedom embracing world-power it manifests external and inner-external being; that emission gradually causes the birth of beings from Brahma-knowers to inert things, manifesting inert and non-inert variety, and also makes the birth of truth when the false world of being is dissolved.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo'dhyātmamucyate | bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ | bṛhatvādbṛṃhakatvācca paraṃ brahma | ata eva  adhyātmaśabdavācyam | yataḥ svaḥ-anivṛttadharmā caitanyākhyo  bhāvaḥ | tasya ca caitanyasvabhāvasya  brahmaṇo'paricchinnabāhyalakṣaṇatayā  kroḍīkṛtaviśvaśakteraiśvaryalakṣaṇātsvātantryāt  bahirbhāvāvabhāsanātmā bahirbhūtabhāvāntarāvabhāsanātmā ca  yo visargaḥ krameṇa bhūtānāṃ-brahmādipramātṝṇāṃ  bhāvānāṃ-jaḍānām udbhavakārī-jaḍājaḍavaicitryanirbhāsakaḥ | tathā bhūtabhāvasya-vigalitasakalavitathaprapañcasya satyatvasya  udbhavaṃ karotīti

plain_english: The perishable is the realm of beings; the person is the divine ground of all gods; and I alone am the sacrifice-overlord here in the body, best of embodied beings. Thus two questions are settled at once, while the remaining question is how you are to be known at the time of departure.
sanskrit_cite: adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivatam | adhiyajño'hamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara | kṣarati-sravati pariṇāmādidharmeṇeti kṣaraḥ-ghaṭādiḥ  padārthagrāma ucyate | puruṣaḥ-ātmā sa cādhidaivatam-tatra  sarvadevatānāṃ pariniṣṭhitatvāt | ata evāśeṣayajñabhoktṛtvena  yajñān-avaśyakāryāṇi karmāṇi adhikṛtya yaḥ sthitaḥ  puruṣottamaḥ so'hameva | ahameva ca dehe sthita iti  praśnadvayamekena yatnena nirṇītam | atha yo'vaśiṣṭaḥ praśnaḥ kathaṃ prayāṇakāle jñeyo'si iti  taṃ nirṇayati-

plain_english: At the time of death, whoever remembers me alone and leaves the body goes to my state; there is no doubt about this.
sanskrit_cite: antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram | yaḥ prayāti sa  madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ

plain_english: Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body at death, that is the state one attains, O Kaunteya, being always imbued with that state.
sanskrit_cite: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram | taṃ tamevaiti  kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight, with mind and intellect offered to Me; you will reach Me without doubt. This is not limited to a stable condition, but applies even at death, since constant cultivation of the Lord's nature brings remembrance of Him then.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca | madarpitamanobuddhirmāmevaiṣyasyasaṃśayam | na kevalaṃ svasthāvasthāyāṃ yāvadantakāle'pi  māmeveti-vyavacchinna-sakalopādhikam | kathaṃ cāsvasthāvasthāyāṃ  vinivṛttasakalendriyaceṣṭasya bhagavān  smṛtipathamupeyāt-ityupāyamapi upadiśati-sarvāvasthāsu  vyāvahārikīṣvapi yasya bhagavattattvaṃ na hṛdayādapayāti tasya  bhagavatyeva sakalakarmasaṃnyāsinaḥ satataṃ bhagavanmayasyāvaśyaṃ  svayameva bhagavattattvam. smṛtiviṣayatāṃ yātīti | sadā  tadbhāvabhāvitatvaṃ cātra hetuḥ | ata evāha-yenaiva vastunā sadā  bhāvitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ plain_english: By yoga of practice, with a mind that does not wander elsewhere, one reaches the supreme divine Person, O Partha, by thinking of him; after the body breaks, freed from bodily pain, one then thinks of the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: abhyāsayogayuktena cetasānanyagāminā | paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ  yāti pārthānucintayan | 8- 8 | anucintayanniti śarīrabhedānantaraṃ nivṛttakalevarakṛtavyathaḥ  paścādbhagavantaṃ cintayanniti

plain_english: He who remembers the seer, the ancient orderer, subtler than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, sun-colored, beyond darkness.
sanskrit_cite: kaviṃ purāṇamanuśāsitāra maṇoraṇīyāṃsamanusmaredyaḥ | sarvasya dhātāramacintyarūpa mādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt

plain_english: At the time of departure, with steady mind and devotion, endowed with yoga power, having properly fixed the breath between the eyebrows, he attains that supreme divine person. Thus one should remember: the Vasudeva principle is sun-colored, transcending the darkness of delusion, likened to the sun; between the eyebrows, as before.
sanskrit_cite: prayāṇakāle manasācalena bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva | bhruvormadhye prāṇamāveśya samyak sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣamupaiti  divyam | evamanusmarediti | ādityavarṇamiti-ādityavarṇatvaṃ  vāsudevatattvasya  paricchedakam-ākṛtikalpanādivibhrāntimayamohatamaso'tītatvāt  ravitvena upamānamityāśayaḥ | bhruvormadhye-iti prāgvat

plain_english: That imperishable which the knowers of the Veda speak of, which ascetics free from attachment enter, and desiring which they practice brahmacarya—I will declare that state to you in summary; rightly grasped and determined by this, summary is the means; by that means I will declare that state here; for constant practice I will speak.
sanskrit_cite: yadakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti viśanti yadyatayo vītarāgāḥ | yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tatte padaṃ saṃgraheṇābhidhāsye | samyag gṛhyate-niścīyate'neneti saṃgrahaḥ-upāyaḥ | tenopāyena  tatpadam abhidhāsye-upāyamatra satatābhyāsāya vakṣye

plain_english: Having restrained all the senses, blocked the mind in the heart, and established the breath—self's charioteer—in the crown beyond all principles by will-power, one practices yoga concentration; this is bodily discipline, where 'in the heart' means freedom from attachment to sense objects rather than mere abiding in a bodily station.
sanskrit_cite: sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca | mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām | dvārāṇi-indriyāṇi | hṛdi-ityanena viṣayasaṃgābhāva ucyate natu  viṣṭhāsthānādhiṣṭhānam | ātmanaḥ prāṇam-ātmasārathim  icchāśaktyātmani mūrdhni-sakalatattvātīte dhārayanniti  kāyaniyamaḥ

plain_english: He who departs uttering Om, the single syllable Brahman, remembering me, goes to the supreme goal.
sanskrit_cite: omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran | yaḥ prayāti  tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim

plain_english: The single-minded yogi who constantly remembers the Lord is easily attained by him; departure is not the decisive factor.
sanskrit_cite: ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ | tasyāhaṃ  sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ | omiti japanniti vāṅniyamaḥ | māmanusmaranniti cetaso'nanyagāmitā | yaḥ prayāti-dināddinamapunarāvṛttaye gacchati | tathā ca-dehaṃ  tyajan-kathaṃ me punaridaṃ sakalāpatsthānaṃ śarīraṃ mā  bhūyāt-ityevaṃ yo māmananyacetāḥ smarati satatameva yātijānāti  sa madbhāvam | natvatra muneḥ paraṃbrahmādvaitapadopakṣepavirodhī  utkrāntau bharaḥ | tathā coktaṃ   vyāpinyāṃ śivasattāyāmutkrāntirnāma niṣphalā | avyāpini śive  nāma notkrāntiḥ śivadāyinī | iti | yadi vā satatābhyāso'pi yairna kṛtastathāpi  kutaścitsvatantreśvarecchādernimittādantye eva kṣaṇe yadā  tādṛgbhāvo jāyate tadāyamutkrāntilakṣaṇa upāyaḥ  saṃskārāntarapratibandhaka uktaḥ | ata eva yadakṣaraṃ vedavido  vadanti ityādinā abhidhāsye ityantena pratijñā kṛtā  kṣaṇamātrasyāpi bhagavadanucintanasya  sakalasaṃskāravidhvaṃsanalakṣaṇāmadbhutavṛttiṃ pratipādayitum | yadāhurācāryavaryāḥ   nimeṣamapi yadyekaṃ kṣīṇadoṣe kariṣyasi | padaṃ citte tadā  śaṃbho kiṃ na saṃpādayiṣyasi | (sta0 ciṃ0 ślo0 114)   iti | ata eva prayāṇakāle smaraṇena vinā khaṇḍanā-iti yeṣāṃ  śaṅkā tān vītaśaṅkānkartumuktam-ananyacetāḥ satatamiti-anyatra  phalādau sādhye yasya na ceta ityarthaḥ | tasyāhaṃ sulabha  iti-tasya na kiṃcitprayāṇakālaucityaparyeṣaṇam-tīrthasevā  uttarāyaṇam āyatanasaṃśrayaḥ sattvavivṛddhiḥ sacintakatvaṃ  viṣuvadādi-puṇyakālaḥ dinam akṛtrimapavitrabhūparigrahaḥ  snehamalavihīnadehatā  śuddhavastrādi-grahaḥ-ityādikleśo'bhyarthanīya ityarthaḥ | yatprāguktaṃ-tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā-ityādi | nanu madbhāvaṃ yāti-ityuktam | tatkiṃ prāpte'pi punarāvṛttirasti  ? ityāśaṅkyāha-

plain_english: Having attained me, great souls do not return to the impermanent abode of suffering; elsewhere return remains.
sanskrit_cite: māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam | napnuvanti  mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ | anyatastu sarvata eva punarāvṛttirastīti samanantareṇa ślokena  pratipāda-yiṣyate | māṃ tu prāpya na punaryogino  janmāditrāsamāpnuvanti

plain_english: All worlds up to Brahma return; attaining the Lord, there is no rebirth.
sanskrit_cite: ābrahma bhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino'rjuna | māmupetya tu kaunteya  punarjanma na vidyate | brahmalokamāptānāmapi punarāvṛttirasti-iti sarvairvyākhyātam | etadabhyupa-game ca taduparitanalokagatirmuktiḥ-ityabhihitaṃ syāt | tacca na hṛdayaṃgamam iti  saṃśayamahāmohakaluṣīkṛtāntarduśāmasmākaṃ  pratibhātīyamāgamādhigatā vyākhyāvarttiḥ ābrahma-yāvat  brahmapadaṃ prāptaṃ tāvat  yasmātkasmāccittiryagūrdhvādhastātbhuvanāt  punarāvartante-cakravatsthānāntaramavirataṃ bhrābhyanto  viparivartante iti | nanu ka evaṃ jānāti yatsarvabhuvanebhyaḥ punarāvṛttiḥ | brahmādaya eva hi tāvacciratarasthāyinaḥ śrūyante | te eva  tāvatkathaṃ punarāvartinaḥ | punarāvartitve hi te'pi syuḥ  prabhavāpyayadharmāṇaḥ ? ityāha-

plain_english: They know Brahma's day as a thousand yugas and night as a thousand yugas.
sanskrit_cite: sahasrayugaparyantamaharye brahmaṇo viduḥ | rātriṃ  yugasahasrāntāṃ te'horātravido janāḥ

plain_english: All manifest beings arise from the unmanifest at day and dissolve into the unmanifest at night.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame | rātryāgame  pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṃjñake

plain_english: The host of beings repeatedly arises and dissolves; the same living beings recur, with time making the difference of long or short cognition, and return is from everywhere except reaching the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate | rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame | ye khalu dīrghadṛśvānaste brahmaṇo'pi rātriṃ dinaṃ paśyanti  pralayodayatayā | tathāca | aharahasta eva vibudhya nijāṃ nijāmeva  ceṣṭāmanurudhyante | pratirātri ca teṣāmeva  nivṛttaparispandānāṃ śaktimātratvenāvasthānam | evaṃ sṛṣṭau  pralaye ca punaḥ punarbhāvaḥ | nānye'nye upasṛjyante apitu te eva  jīvāḥ kālakṛtastu cirakṣiprapratyayātmā viśeṣaḥ | eṣa ca  paricchedaḥ prajāpatīnāmapyasti | tataśca te'pi  prabhavāpyayadharmāṇa eva-iti sthitam | sarvato lokebhyaḥ punarāvṛttirnatu māṃ prāpya iti sphuṭayati-

plain_english: Beyond that is another eternal being, manifest and unmanifest, which does not perish when all beings perish.
sanskrit_cite: parastasmāttu bhāvo'nyo vyaktāvyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ | yaḥ sa  sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati

plain_english: The unmanifest imperishable is called the supreme goal; reaching it there is no return, and that supreme abode is mine.
sanskrit_cite: avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim | yaṃ prāpya na  nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama

plain_english: The supreme person is attainable by unwavering devotion; reaching him there is no rebirth, beings stand within him, and a distinction is stated for those desiring enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā | yaṃ prāpya  na punarjanma labhante yogino'rjuna | yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yatra sarva pratiṣiṭhatam | uktaprakāraṃ kālasaṃkalanāvivarjitaṃ tu vāsudevatattvam | vyaktam-sarvānugatam tattve'pi avyaktaṃ-duṣprāpatvāt | tacca  bhaktilabhyamityāveditaṃ prāk | tatrasthaṃ caitadviśvam | yat  khalvavināśi rūpaṃ sadā tathābhūtaṃ tatra kaḥ  punaḥśabdasyāvṛttiśabdasya cārthaḥ | sa hi madhye  tatsvabhāvavicchedāpekṣaḥ | na ca  sadātanaviśvottīrṇaviśvāvyatiriktaviśvapratiṣṭhātmakaparabodha  svātantrya-svabhāvasya śrīparameśvarasya tadbhāvaprāptiḥ yena  svabhāvavicchedaḥ ko'pi kadāpyasti | ato yuktamuktaṃ-māmupetya  tu-iti | evaṃ ca satatābhyāsena yeṣāṃ kleśaṃ vinaiva  bhagavadāptisteṣāṃ vṛttamuktam idānīmutkrāntyā ye'pavargaṃ  bhogaṃ cecchanti teṣāṃ kaścidviśeṣa ucyate-

plain_english: Departing yogis go to non-return or return; the time for this will be spoken, non-return being liberation and return being for enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ | prayātā yānti  taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha | anāvṛttiḥ-mokṣaḥ | āvṛttiḥ-bhogāya

plain_english: Departing knowers of brahman in the bright six-month northern course go to brahman.
sanskrit_cite: agnijyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam | tatra prayātā  gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ

plain_english: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the southern course mark the path by which the yogi reaches lunar light and returns; the opposite northern course is light-natured and leads to non-return.
sanskrit_cite: dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam | tatra  cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate | uttareṇa-ūrdhvena ayanaṃ-ṣāṇmāsikam | tacca  prakāśādidharmakatvāt dahanādikaiḥ śabdairupacaryate | ato  viparītaṃ viparyayeṇa | tatra candramaso  bhogyāṃśānupraveśādbhogāyāvṛttiḥ

plain_english: These white and black paths are the world's eternal courses; by one one goes to non-return, by the other one returns for enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate | anayoryātyanāvṛttimādyayāvartate'nyayā | anayorgatyormadhyādādyayā-anāvṛttiḥ-mokṣaḥ | anyayā bhogaḥ

plain_english: No knowing yogi is deluded by these paths; therefore be yoga-joined in all times, Arjuna.
sanskrit_cite: naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana | tasmātsarveṣu  kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna | ete sṛtī yo vetti-ābhyantareṇa krameṇa  yogābhyāsasvīkṛtenetyarthaḥ | etacca vitatya prakāśyamānaṃ  granthaṃ vistārayatītyalam | sarve ye kālā ābhyantarāḥ  tadviṣayaṃ yogamabhyasyet | asmadguravastvāhuḥ-sarvānugrāhakatayā  madhye ābhyantarakālakṛtamutkrāntibhedamabhidhāya prakṛtameva  bāhyakālaviṣayaṃ mukhyaṃ prameyamupasaṃhṛtam tasmātsarveṣu  kāleṣu-ityādinā

plain_english: Knowing all declared merit, the yogi reaches the supreme place and, through remembrance of the Lord, easily finds supreme Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam | abhyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam | abhyeti-abhibhavati-sarvakarmasaṃskārāṇāṃ bhagavatsmṛtyā  viphalīkaraṇāt | sarvakarmaparikṣaye cāsau sukhenaiva vindati  paraṃ śivamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: when all principles are known in the supreme Lord, there is no inside-or-outside condition in which the all-pervading shines.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   sarvatattvagatatvena vijñāte parameśvare | antarbahirna sāvasthā na  yasyāṃ bhāsate vibhuḥ | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe'ṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ
